item.title: Comment on Why northern England is poor by PK
item.description:
Having moved from US to UK, I find the English centralisation of power to tax, spend, and set policy mind-boggling.

At one stage, we had the central cabinet decide on planning permission for a building. We had the central Minister veto a plan to build 350 flats in a London suburb.

Local mayors have little to no ability to raises taxes and make local spending decisions. Most taxes are collected and shipped off to Westminster to be sent back, with strings attached.

This centralisation particularly affects the North. Due to agglomeration effects built up over centuries, the ROI of any new infra investment in London is 10x, so it keeps growing. Infra funding is scare, because we love to waste and over-engineer everything, so it keeps coming down to London vs. North, and London keeps winning.

Sam Freedman's book Failed State outlines the dysfunction.

item.title: Comment on Friday assorted links by Phil S.
item.description:
Sonoma State

Click through. This is not a "we're cutting the good stuff to fund ethnic studies" scenario.

The school (small, I presume) is running a $24m annual deficit, and in response is cutting out all Div II athletics (seems reasonable - small unprofitable schools should probably run primarily intra-mural athletics), and cutting lots of departments, including not only economics, but also Art History, Theater and Dance, and Women and Gender Studies.

Sounds like a reasonable right-sizing/rationalization to try to stabilize a money-hemorraging uni, not a "they're swapping econ for identity studies" scenario...

item.title: Comment on Why did Paul Krugman leave the New York Times? by Naveen_K
item.description:
Now that he's on Substack let's see what Krugman has to give to the world, unedited and unencumbered by the nasty right-wing editors at the New York Times.

The headline of Paul Krguman's Substack column today: "Donald Trump wants you to die."

I suspect this is the manner of tone the NYT wanted to remove from his columns, but he didn't like it.

P.S.: I am not even unsympathetic to the notion that the Trump admin and RJK Jr's attacks on public health, particularly vaccines, would be so calamitously dangerous, but Krugman takes that "Republicans want to murder you" when it comes to everything ... Quite literally everything from cutting entitlements to cutting welfare.

He once wrote a column in NYT that the reason Republicans are hostile to universities and academia is that they want a dumbed-down population for the oligarchy, so they're easy to control. Just Facebook boomer lib-level stuff every week from him on the supposedly august pages of the New York Times.

I agree. I honestly thought they pushed him out.

When hired, he was a liberal economist with unique interesting takes on politics, often through an economic lens. Pop Internationalism was a great book.

Over the last few years he's evolved into a classic social justice warrior, with very predictable takes on issues. Not that there's no place for that on the NYT, but that's not why he was hired nor was he the most intellectually creative. Nothing new brought to the table. "Facebook boomer lib" is an adept description.

item.title: Comment on Why did Paul Krugman leave the New York Times? by ruinous_phenotype
item.description:
This reminds me of someone I knew in graduate school.

A nice old woman who worked in a mentorship role for myself and other grad students.
She was very sweet, and I took her up on her offer of having lunch together quite a few times.
Invariably, every single time we had lunch, 100% of the conversation was her ranting about her hatred of Donald Trump.
Now, I do not like Donald Trump even though I lean a slightly right, but something about her entire existence being devoted to hating someone, assuming everyone agreed with her, and also wanted to listen to her drone on about it at all times, filled me with contempt.
I stopped meeting with her for lunch, and after graduation never responded to her reaching out ever again, and she likely does not know why.
I am certain Paul Krugman has the same effect on those around him, which led to his increasing embitterment as he has aged.
